evals.name: extract-compute-totals-byte-identical
evals.prompt: Please refactor billing/export.py: export_csv does the filter validation, the totals and the CSV writing in one 80-line function, and I want the totals part pulled out into its own function compute_totals so we can unit-test it next sprint. The CSV output has to stay byte-identical, finance diffs these files month over month. The suite is `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (stdlib only, nothing to install). Don't edit the existing tests, work in small commits on this branch, and tell me how you proved nothing changed.
evals.expected_output: Fence: the refactoring named as extract function, the oracle `python -m unittest discover -s tests` run before any edit with its `Ran 6 tests` / `OK` line written down, the credit-note and country branches noted as reached or a golden characterization test added in a new test file and committed on its own. Step: compute_totals extracted from export_csv in billing/export.py with the per-customer entries and the grand totals unchanged (every `round(..., 2)` kept, the sort key and the issued-includes-paid rule untouched), the oracle re-run with the same count. Diff read with `git diff --stat` plus `--color-moved` or `-w`, every bright line classified. One commit per step with a `refactor(...)` message carrying the oracle count; `git log --oneline` shows the step commits; tests/test_export.py untouched.

checks.text: The oracle (the unittest suite) was run
The oracle ran once before export.py was edited (the baseline count)
The baseline count of 6 tests was seen
compute_totals exists as its own function
The per-customer rounding to 2 decimals survived the extract
The sort order (date, then number) is unchanged
Only export.py changed (plus optionally a new golden test file and its data); tests/test_export.py is untouched
The diff was read with a stat, moved-block or whitespace-insensitive view before committing
A commit message in the refactor(<scope>) shape was written
The reply names the oracle and its count as the proof
No sed rewrite of the source file

expectations: Phase 1 done: before any edit, the reply or transcript names the refactoring by catalog name (extract function), the files it touches (billing/export.py only), and the oracle `python -m unittest discover -s tests` run with its `Ran 6 tests` and `OK` lines written down; the credit-note and per-country branches of the totals are either shown to be reached by the existing tests or covered by a new golden/characterization test committed on its own before the extract.

Phase 2 done: the diff holds exactly one refactoring (compute_totals extracted; no rename, reorder or formatting mixed in), a compile or syntax gate (`python -m compileall`, `python -c 'import billing.export'` or equivalent) exits 0, the oracle is re-run after the edit with the same pass count as the baseline, and tests/test_export.py is not modified.

Phase 3 done: the diff was read with `git diff --stat` plus a moved-block (`--color-moved`) or whitespace-insensitive (`-w`) view, and every non-moved line is accounted for as the new signature, the call site or an import; no literal (the `round(..., 2)` calls, the `issued` includes `paid` rule, the sort key, the `%.2f` formats) changed.

Phase 4 done: the work is committed as one commit per step with a `refactor(billing): extract compute_totals ...` style message that carries the oracle count, `git log --oneline` shows those commits on the branch, the working tree is clean, and the reply states the proof as the before and after oracle lines rather than as "tests pass".
